items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Lionel Hampton, So, we’re all bandleaders in there, you know, and every place that we have gone, it’s been a success, a tremendous success.

ctx.x: Was there ever a time where you went face to face, a battle with the Ellington band?

I can’t say that we did. We did with the Lionel Hampton band. He always wanted to choose Basie because he said his band was better than Basie’s band, we could swing better and everything. So, we just had it out at the Savoy one night. And he never did do that anymore. But you were well entertained when you would go to the Savoy and you had Chick Webb, Teddy Hill, and they had a little group up there called the Savoy Sultans and they’d wear you out. There was only about eight of them but they sounded like 80.…
And you were playing virtually exclusively for dancing, correct?

items.title: Harry "Sweets" Edison interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: I’m going to the Hollywood Bowl... a tribute to Lionel Hampton... And I’m going to the Kennedy Center on the 8th to play a concert there for the President with Lionel Hampton.

ctx.x: Tell us about what you’re doing today.

For the future? Well I’m not going on the road no three hundred one-nighters anymore that’s for sure. I’m through with that. But I have, I’m going to Chicago in the morning to play a festival with Clark Terry. And the 13th I’ll be at the Hollywood Bowl, the last jazz series of the summer, a tribute to Lionel Hampton which is called “Vibes.” And I’m going to the Kennedy Center on the 8th to play a concert there for the President with Lionel Hampton. And I’m going to Europe, going to Paris at a place called the…

items.title: Lionel Hampton interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: We’ve got Sweets Edison playing one trumpet, and we’ve got Al Grey playing trombone

ctx.x: Buddy Tate is not playing. But maybe it will come to me after. We’ve got Sweets Edison playing one trumpet, and we’ve got Al Grey playing trombone and oh, this is all changed up.
Yeah. You’ve got Junior Mance on piano?
